text: The public Solana RPC endpoints are rate-limited and are not meant for production. The Solana docs say they are 'not intended for production applications', that limits may change without prior notice, and that high-traffic websites may be blocked without prior notice. The Velocity and Drift gateway READMEs say api.mainnet-beta.solana.com is 'not recommend for production use cases'. Kamino's SDK docs say the SDK needs 'a private RPC connection or the public rate-limited RPC endpoint'. OnFinality, an RPC provider, calls public endpoints heavily rate-limited and advises a dedicated endpoint. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
keywords: Rate limits auth and RPC requirements

text: The /swap/v2/execute endpoint has its own rate-limit bucket, separate from the main limit: Keyless 20 RPS, Free 50 RPS, and 100 RPS for Developer, Launch and Pro. Execute calls cost 0 credits and do not count against the main bucket, so a Developer organisation can make 10 main requests and 100 /execute requests in the same second. Heavy /order polling therefore does not throttle transaction landing. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
keywords: Rate limits auth and RPC requirements

text: VelocityClient reads account state in one of three modes, and each puts a different load on the RPC. Websocket is the default and pushes updates per account, but many RPC endpoints cap concurrent subscriptions. Polling uses BulkAccountLoader(connection, commitment, pollingFrequencyMs) to batch getMultipleAccounts calls, which gives predictable request volume on any RPC. The grpc mode uses a Yellowstone/Geyser stream and needs a gRPC-enabled provider such as Jito or Triton, an auth token, and usually a paid plan. Helius gates gRPC the same way: LaserStream gRPC is off on Free, devnet-only on Developer, and on for Business and Professional. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
keywords: Rate limits auth and RPC requirements
